text:
The key question ahead of the Fed meeting today was if economic activity is strengthening and broadening, inflation remains elevated, and most people think rates need to go up again, why wait until December?

Here's how Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh asked the question (put to him by @colbyLsmith of the NYT). 

Boiled down, his answer suggested the Fed has built enough credibility that waiting six weeks costs little, so they’ll take the extra information. He never says that outright. Most of the answer offered a defense of his record rather than a rationale for this decision.

text:
Former Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat to a student-led opposition movement in Serbia’s October 25 parliamentary elections, ending his party’s 14 years in power.

The vote came after nearly 2 years of student-led protests sparked by the deaths of 16 people when a canopy collapsed at a renovated railway station, a disaster that protesters blamed on corruption and cronyism.

“The student movement now has wind in its sails and lots of political momentum,” expert @CharlesKupchan, who was in Belgrade days before the vote, said. “It needs to focus on turning that momentum into good policies and good governance.”
